Scaling

Automatically adjust compute capacity to meet demand.

1. Core Concept

  • Auto Scaling Groups (ASGs) ensure you always have the right number of instances running. They kill unhealthy instances and spin up new ones based on CPU, network, or custom metrics.

2. Key Services & Features

  • Launch Templates:
    • Defines what to launch: AMI, instance type, security groups, SSH key, and user data script.
    • Supports versioning (unlike deprecated Launch Configurations).
  • Auto Scaling Group (ASG):
    • Defines where and how to launch: Subnets (VPC), Min/Max/Desired capacity.
    • Integrates with ALB target groups to automatically register new instances.
  • Scaling Policies:
    • Target Tracking: 'Keep average CPU at 50%'.
    • Step Scaling: Add exactly 2 instances when alarm breaches.
    • Scheduled: Scale up Friday at 8 AM.

3. Architecture Rules

  • Always configure ASGs to span multiple Availability Zones for fault tolerance.
  • Use Target Tracking policies for the simplest, most reliable scaling logic.
  • Use Lifecycle Hooks to pause instances for custom setup scripts or draining before termination.

4. Scenarios & Use Cases

  • Traffic spikes unpredictably, causing EC2 instances to crash from CPU overload.
    • Choose: ASG with Target Tracking scaling policy.
    • Why: It dynamically adds compute capacity precisely when metrics rise, and removes it when they drop.
  • A retail site knows traffic will quadruple every Black Friday at midnight.
    • Choose: Scheduled Scaling.
    • Why: Predictive spikes should be provisioned ahead of time rather than waiting for reactive metrics to trip.

Q1 A user is aware that a huge download is occurring on his instance. He has already set the Auto Scaling policy to increase the instance count when the network I/O increases beyond a certain limit. How can the user ensure that this temporary event does not result in scaling?
  • A The network I/O are not affected during data download.
  • B The policy cannot be set on the network I/O.
  • C There is no way the user can stop scaling as it is already configured.
  • D Suspend scaling.
Answer: D

Q20 A media startup is designing a workload on AWS. The architecture needs to run a stateless web tier that scales automatically across Availability Zones with the least operational overhead. Which solution should be selected?
  • A EC2 Auto Scaling behind an Application Load Balancer
  • B A single NAT gateway
  • C Amazon Route 53 Resolver only
  • D One large EC2 instance with an Elastic IP
Answer: A

An ALB distributes HTTP traffic while Auto Scaling adjusts instance capacity.

Q24 Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework includes the principle "Stop guessing your capacity needs"?
  • A Cost Optimization
  • B Performance Efficiency
  • C Reliability
  • D Operational Excellence
Answer: B

- Performance Efficiency pillar includes capacity planning principles - "Stop guessing capacity" - use Auto Scaling and elastic services - Enables right-sizing and dynamic capacity adjustment - Cost Optimization focuses on eliminating waste - Reliability focuses on recovery and testing - Operational Excellence focuses on running/monitoring
